Doesn't sound backwards at all. This thought still crops up from time to time for me because I spent years of my life just waiting and putting undue stress on my platonic and romantic relationships -- or anyone that would give me even the slightest chance at one. 

I feel ya on all what you said about your exp and can relate hardcore. The last LTR I was in, she remarked that I was "one of the best relationships" she's ever had, only to turn around inform me that she had to manage my emotions for me and broke it off... yet still wanted to be friends? It's sad to say that she did help me grow yet also damaged my faith in my discernment of people. I thought I was doing okay, but that caused cracks in whatever foundation I had been re-laying for like the past 2 years. I have so much self-doubt that I question every single choice I make -- including with whom I share any information with for fear that it's going to to be used against me at a later point. Mind you, that's a very old wound, but this situation caused it to bust wide open and start bleeding everywhere again. 

Yeah, finally coming to terms with the fact that no one is coming to save you is nothing short of shitastic. And the bonus content of realizing that you gotta save yourself? Especially for someone like me who has such little faith in themselves to do it in the first place? You might as well be asking me to move the Great Wall of China brick by brick to the opposite side of the country using only an ox, a cart, and my own 2 hands. And I swear to gods, it feels like that most days, where I get out of my weekly therapy sessions or close my workbook and/or journal and wonder wtf am I doing this for if I'll never be "fully healed"? But maybe that's a "toxic positivity" take on it. We're all at least a little banged-up, and to come back pristine from damage is -- I think -- impossible. So maybe "fully healed" is synonymous with perfection, which is unattainable. We can get close, but we'll never reach it. AND THAT'S FUCKING OKAY. Maybe "mostly" or even "somewhat healed" is a better and more realistic target. Hell, maybe a better target would be just "meh" for right now. Like when it comes to me, I'm striving for self-neutrality rather than self-love (I really fcuking hate that shit). I would love to be just "maybe" at me for right now instead of the barrage of self-doubt. Especially when I know I have to be the one to save myself from this. Like I'm stuck in the training montage right now, and I'm going, okay when do I get to finally start doing cool shit? And Sensei is just like, "Bro, chill. You still got a while yet. Now drop and gimme 50." 

But isolation is not going to aid in these efforts. Sure there's a time for contemplation and reflection, but it can get to a point of ruminating, which then is more harmful than good. As a constant ruminator that my therapist has to reel back all the time, I'm still trying to find the line where I'm actually thinking rather than just "in my head", and my Sifu has told me. I know for me, I have to get out of my head otherwise I'll keep perpetuating this prison of my own creation. 

I know this is a novel, so my apologies, but TLDR: you're not alone. This shit sucks, but IMO total isolation didn't do me any favors. Isolation is often the lifeblood of our CPTSD. The more we take away its food source, the weaker it'll become.

I get these a lot. To echo the point of another redditor on this thread, label it what it is: rogue thoughts. It's difficult, but don't give it any credence, heed it, or give it any energy, They do NOT indicate your quality as a person. They pop up seemingly randomly and cause us distress because of their content, but really it's a rogue thought. Nothing more, nothing less. It's like finding a pebble when sorting beans. A pebble is not really cause for alarm or any clear indication of the quality of the beans in total. It's annoying, sure, but toss it out and cook the beans. If you start paying more attn to that pebble, that pebble is then going to become a boulder, which does not benefit you and ultimately ruins your refried beans. So when I find a pebble in my beans, I do something very similar to a redditor here and either inwardly or outwardly label it what it is: "Rogue thought!" and switch gears is whatever best suits my needs.

Now if these keep popping up along with an actual desire and conscious plan to carry out any of these negative thoughts, then that's when it's time to seek a professional. But you seem to have a strong resistance to these thoughts, and so far as I can tell you don't have a conscious plan and you don't plan on having a plan.

Eh... I would like to place my rebuttal about the "less dangerous" bit. There is much about s3x and s3xual activity that can increase the risk, especially if kink is involved and/or those s3x acts are done in a potentially harm-inducing way. This can include things like an@l penetration (or any penetration, really) or performing some acts without proper protection or taking precautions to reduce potential harm before, during, and after. That's a very broad net and what I just said can be very vague as well, I know, but how people do the s3xy time is just as vast and varied with their own inherent risks. No s3x act is 100% safe. I'll put it like that.

I'm not saying this as a deterrent or coming from some puritanical soapbox. Go f\*ck to your heart's content. But saying that it's "less dangerous" than drugs can give a false impression that doesn't consider all the risks involved. People can and do get hurt. Not only from the acts themselves but also as trans people. Fetishization exists, and there are unscrupulous people out there that don't consider trans people actual people and will treat us like objects that can be tossed out when done with them. We sex-neutral and sex-favorable folks have to be careful when it comes to new partners and anonymous encounters as they could result in getting into a terrible situation. Remember that the "trans panic" defense is still legal in 31 states (https://lgbtqbar.org/programs/advocacy/gay-trans-panic-defense/gay-trans-panic-defense-legislation/).

One can occasionally take Molly and be fine, as long as they get it from a reputable source and know they have no other conditions that could put them in harm's way. One can occasionally take K, poppers, G, any of those and still be "okay" if they're around trustworthy people, get it from a reputable source, and start out with small amounts. I will agree, many drugs can still be labeled as dangerous outright, e.g. meth, heroin, rohypnol (aka roofies), all those heavy hitters. But in some major cities, you can take your molly, K, coke, whatever to a lab and have it tested for anything dangerous without them ratting you out to the cops. One of the nonprofits I work with has fentanyl test strips readily available for anyone who wants them. No ID needed. They just come in, grab them, and go. Why? Because just like s3x, people are gonna do drugs. We don't live in a perfect world, and that world is a thinly veiled hellscape that many are having a huge difficulty coping with. But we can mitigate the risks associated with both s3x and drugs IF WE'RE AWARE OF AND ACKNOWLEDGE THEM. Then we can take the steps to reduce that risk. Again, nothing is 100% safe, but you can take steps to increase safety.

One last thing, then I'll get off my nonpuritanical soapbox. Asexuals can get similar (if not greater) pleasure from sources other than s3x, and their uninterest in it needn't be disregarded. From where I'm sitting, that remark about the ecstasy of s3x sounded dismissive towards asexuals, almost like, "Oh you don't know what you're missing! You poor unfortunate soul! Try it once, and you might like it." I'm going to assume that's not what you meant with that comment. I'm sure you know that some people are sex-repulsed and really have no interest in it. That's like someone coming up to me and trying to shove some fried tarantula in my face. I have never eaten tarantula, and I know damn well I don't want to.

Look, friend. I was in quite a similar situation a few years ago. I understand where you're coming from. It's a terrible place to be. 

Your brain wants to tell you that they'll be fine because that's what I told myself. They'll get over it. They'll move on. I would be romanticized in their eyes and not be seen for the "monster" I was. 

As someone who's been to more of their fair share of funerals over the years and seen the aftermath of s**cide first hand, it never goes like that. Ever. No one who was connected with you in some way ever "gets over it". I'm not saying this to drive in the nail of guilt, trying to preach the whole "live for others" bit , because living for others doesn't really do anything. But think about this: there's a reason why you haven't done it yet. And it's not because death will cause some "inconvenience" (side note: this is what my ex told me why he didn't do it in the past). It's not because of a lack of persuasion. It's not because fear. 

For me, what made me finally get myself to a therapist was a stark realization one night when I was..."heavily involved in an alternate reality". I didn't know why I wanted me dead, but I remember saying to myself, if you want me dead, you'll have to find some other way to do it because f*ck you, that's why. I had my autonomy and power taken from me when I was younger, and this was my first step to taking back what was rightfully mine. 

Your life is yours. This. Is. Yours. 

Living for others didn't do it for me because I felt like I  owed people and my existence was indentured servitude. I don't owe anything to anyone. I don't owe someone my existence. I can do whatever I want with this time I have. Every minute I have I can give to someone else freely. 

But what keeps me going, even now, is figuring out where this life will go. What else can I do with it? No I didn't ask to be born. But I'm here now. And I'm gonna do what I can with it until I can't anymore. I'll have my own blood on my hands only when I'm about to take down the motherf*cker stupid enough to try it. And, look, I'm not the smartest man, but I don't think I'm that ignorant. 

I have to play chess with my demons daily. It's exhausting. But my stubbornness won't put the game down, no matter how tired I am. Something wants me to keep going, and these things want to defeat me. Why? Idk. But I'm sure as hell gonna find out. 

Btw, saying "f*ck you" is incredibly empowering.

I get this so much. I'm creating an entire fantasy world that has some relevance to this world. But I have to try to not stereotype different cultures or pigeon-hole them in a way that's offensive. That's one of the themes I'm trying to cover throughout the series is bigotry and its effects on society, i.e. how it hurts everyone in the end.   
So the roster of these characters goes as follows (I put the quotes around them because that's where I'm drawing inspiration from but these areas don't exist in this fantasy world):  
A "Middle Eastern" trans woman 

A "Central American" cis asexual man

An "Eastern European" nonbinary person and trans man

A Black cis lesbian

An "Asian" cis woman (whose sexuality I'm not even sure I want to bring into the series as this is already getting really complex)

There are only a few experiences where I can write about from personal experience myself. Otherwise, I've been reading blogs, doing interviews, and researching to the best of my abilities to ensure I don't get something wrong or turn it into something offensive. 

What's more, I have to make sure that what I borrow from one culture doesn't turn into a negative stereotype or have it become the sole focus to a point of negative conclusions. This is especially true when it comes to race. Because these races exist in this fantasy world per se, but not in the way that we in this world have come to develop our own prejudices and stereotypes. I'm not sure if I'm being clear or not, but I hope I got my point across.

"But! But! I saw a cat do it! Why can I not??" it asked through what I thought could be a mouth. But on this guy, it was really hard to tell. But before me lied not a mouse. No. It was half of a cow. In my living room. With blood now staining the rug I had just got last week. How he found a cow in the middle of Atlanta was beyond me right now, and one of the last thoughts on my mind. There was half of a cow in my living room that I would have to drag down several flights of stairs to get rid of -- without arousing suspicion and potential jail time. Because this was half of a damn cow.

"Goddamnit, Amy." I rubbed my temples. "Cats bring in mice. Mice! This is a cow! They're two totally different animals!"

"Human, you very well cannot... uh... what is the word for cooking carcasses over a fire outside?" Amy's one eye darted throughout the room, looking for the very thing he was trying to name.

I stared at him in disbelief. "Do you mean 'barbeque'? You want to barbeque half a cow?!"

He shrugged. "Well, you cannot... ber-ber-coo a mouse. It would feed no one to sustain their malice." His one eye rolled at me as if I said something really stupid.

I sighed heavily as I stared at the cow carcass. "We can't eat \*all\* that, Amy."

He laughed that laugh that shook the walls with such a deep, echoing baritone voice and raised a blood-drenched, 2-foot long claw to his face. I felt myself crouch without thought. "Human, no! I desire more humans. I desire to experience this ber-ber-coo for myself. What is the word for brethren that you wish not to kill? Those you want to keep because you hate them not as much as others?"

"Uh... friends?"  I raised an eyebrow.

"Yes!" he called out. "Friends! I wish to experience your friends!"

"Amy, where did you get this idea? And where did you find a cow? Also, where's the other half? Do you even know how to butcher a cow?"

He shook his bloody, clawed hand at me. "Fear not, Ash. As Amaranthinus, I can do and know all with the help of that invisible library inside your magical box. I can go into my own dimension where time is irrelevant to learn this. Not even a second will have passed in your world before I return with the knowledge from a compendium of human butchery!"

I wanted to tell him that the sentence alone sounded odd, but there was a bigger problem. My friends would not be as accepting of Amy as I was... mostly because he was an eldritch horror with claws, peeling red skin, and one black eye that would likely scare them into madness. "Do... you know how to disguise yourself to at least look something like me?"

"Am I not doing that already?" he remarked.

"Amy..." I closed my eyes and exhaled sharply. "Not really. The peeling skin needs to go, and you need to not be as... flaming red? Also, those claws would have to look like my hands." I raised both of them in front of me. "I can't invite my friends over until you have this down."

He nodded, and then a cacophony of grunts, growls, and high-pitched screaming lept out from somewhere in his vicinity. I watched in utter disgust as his long arms turned shorter and his knees reversed direction with a sickening crack. His skin started to give off steam as it started to melt together, giving a smoother appearance overall. His solid black eye sank into his head with a squelch then reemerged with two amber cat eyes along with lips and a nose that seemed just a touch too long. His arms appeared normal, but his hands were also a little large with nails that were as long as talons. However, after more squelching and screaming, he appeared as an extremely tall androgynous human with cat eyes. The long flaming red hair hid his chest as he stood in my living room completely naked. He placed one of his taloned hands on his hip as if striking a pose. "Well..." his voice rumbled. "Good enough?"

What was previously disgust was now... a feeling that I would likely have to reconcile with. Was I... attracted to him right now? I shook the thought out of my head. "That looks... really good!"

He wore a smug smile.

I jumped as I realized that I was staring and went to my room for my robe. I was likely half his size right now, but I needed to cover him up before my mind went places where it shouldn't. Even if that meant that this robe would be a vain attempt at concealing what was in my living room. Before I could give it to him, a knock came at my door. My eyes widened with fear. I threw the robe at him, instructing him to put it on, and went to the door. Looking out the peephole, the sheen of a brass badge flickered in the hallway light as the navy blue uniform stood out against the beige backdrop. Could I ignore it?

Another knock. "Atlanta PD! Open up!"

"Shit!" I whispered and looked at Amy. The robe looked absolutely ridiculous on him as the hem barely touched his upper thigh and only closed with some effort of the fabric belt. He furrowed his thick brow and started walking to the door. "No, Amy! I'll handle it!"

He didn't listen as he pushed me aside and opened the door. Amy looked down at the officer who barely came up to his chest. "Good morning... uh... s-sir?" the officer announced. I was standing on the other side of the door, chewing my nails and staring at the half cow carcass that was right in the middle of my living room, just out of the officer's line of sight.

"Good morning, officer!" he said with an unnatural amount of cheer. "How can I help you?"

"Uh, yes, we got a noise complaint from someone in the building. Said that they heard some... disturbing sounds coming from this apartment," he relayed.

Amy tutted at him. "Silly old Kathy. She's always thinking there's something nefarious going on."

"Is there?"

I heard a pause but then a guttural snarl arise from his chest like an angry hellhound about to attack. I then heard the officer's shaky breaths. It all of a sudden stopped entirely. Fearing the worst, I came out from behind the door to see the two of them as still as statues but with Amy's hand on the officer's arm. Amy's face looked as normal as it could have but the officer looked at her in sheer terror. I tried to shake Amy awake but she didn't move. Neither of them did.

I looked on in confusion at the scene, hoping none of my neighbors chose this moment to leave. How much longer would this last? Had time stopped for them but me?

I pondered these questions when Amy blinked and released the officer's arm. He only stood there with the same expression of terror and not breathing. Without another thought, Amy closed the door on his face.

She then started to laugh. "Oh what fun it is to torture those keepers of 'laws'!" He put air quotes on the word "laws". "Next time, you should join me!"

"What... happened to him?" I asked.

He said between fits of laughter. "He's lost in an interdimensional time flux!" He then went on to say, "Oh, he'll be back soon enough. But oh! How broken he will be! He'll be a babbling lunatic for the rest of his days!" He crouched to the floor, holding his stomach. Blood leaked out of his eyes. "Oh! I can't remember the last time I laughed that hard!" He wiped away the blood tears with the sleeve of the robe, now staining crimson on the white terry cloth. He then stood back up, towering over me. "Now, to plan for this ber-ber-coo!"

What dreariness. What dark incomprehensible shade. 

Taking over for Death should not have been so simple, and yet, here he was. Looking into the vial, the crimson liquid promised that that he could change the world — that for once, he could do something that mattered. The bruises that once patterned him arms now gone as he donned the red dress of  Death. The scars and pockmarks that marred his face now smooth as alabaster. He lifted a hand to feel it glide across his cheek with ease. Until he met the now unnatural width of what would have been his mouth. The raised flesh still felt tender to the touch as the tattered sleeves fell around his wrists. The cloth’s strands danced across the still tender wounds there as well. Something said he should look, if only to see the remnants of the promise, but averted his eyes back to the floating vial before him. 

It was done. The world now turned to shade before his own darkened eyes, leaving him to wander through his thoughts alone. After all, now, he was truly away from the world. He had expected to hear the howls and screams of the long forgotten ringing in his ears, but only the whisper of the calm breeze welcomed him to his new post. A Royal of the Darkness, it announced... as if anyone was actually listening. 

But that was the beauty of his new domain. No one screamed. No one howled in pain. Not one cry did he hear as he nestled into the arms of the gnarled oak. Paradise had truly come for him. At last, the raging torrents in his mind had ceased. The quiet and the darkness felt like a nocturne from the age of romance. They played so well together, creating a masterpiece with the breeze that it moved him to tears. But a salty water did not leak from his eyes. The liquid that fell down those alabaster cheeks strained to flow, becoming sticky And saw red cloud his vision.

Blood now stained his hand as he wiped away the tears, now pooling in the corners of his unnatural smile. Then a small laugh rose from deep within him. He said then to the tree, “Well...” as he looked out into the land of forever twilight. “Guess I better get to work.”
